connection: Session 23 provides the prerequisite vocabulary. This session develops resource lifetime through a focused TimeLedger change.
objectives: Explain why exceptions propagate until handled, and using guarantees Dispose runs when control leaves a scope through success or failure.

Prove the contract with focused and regression tests.

concept.title: Name the contract
paragraphs: The governing rule is that exceptions propagate until handled, and using guarantees Dispose runs when control leaves a scope through success or failure.
Start with what callers need to know, then keep incidental implementation details behind the boundary.
concept.code:
using OperationScope scope = new(onDispose);
throw new InvalidOperationException();

concept.title: Trace dependencies and control
paragraphs: Follow calls from the public operation through each collaborator or transformation.
A clear direction reduces branching, duplication, and accidental coupling.
concept.code:
// Read the pipeline from caller to result.
using OperationScope scope = new(onDispose);

concept.title: Make behavior executable
paragraphs: Focused tests demonstrate the new rule with small deterministic values.
The complete suite then confirms the cumulative application still honors earlier contracts.

lab.objective: Add a compact TimeLedger example for exception propagation, idisposable, and using.
lab.startingCondition: Sessions 01–23 are complete and all existing tests pass.
steps: Predict the successful path and one boundary or failure case.
Add src/TimeLedger.Domain/OperationScope.cs with a narrow public contract.
Add tests/TimeLedger.Domain.Tests/OperationScopeTests.cs for the prediction and boundary case.
Run the focused tests and inspect the observed values or control flow.
Run the full Release build and test suite.
lab.expectedBehavior: The new tests establish that exceptions propagate until handled, and using guarantees Dispose runs when control leaves a scope through success or failure; prior behavior remains unchanged.
lab.validation: dotnet build TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test TimeLedger.sln --configuration Release

reflections: Which boundary in this session carries the most design responsibility?
How does the test reveal cause and effect rather than just a final value?
What implementation detail can change without affecting callers?
whatBreaks: Removing OperationScope.cs removes the executable model for resource lifetime. Removing its tests permits contract regressions. If the boundary leaks its implementation details, callers become harder to change and isolated testing loses value.
summary: This session established that exceptions propagate until handled, and using guarantees Dispose runs when control leaves a scope through success or failure. The application change and tests preserve that model as executable documentation.
